messages:
oliver_cs: FYI got an urgent message from a customer (Acme) reporting a codegen regression after yesterday's rollout to codegen-2.3q. They say TypeScript output now fails to compile, missing exports and truncated helper functions. Pasting their minimal repro and errors below.

oliver_cs: Customer paste ->

--- begin customer message ---
Hi Redwood,
After the update yesterday our generated SDKs for the user service no longer compile. The function definitions used to include named exports and an exported helper, now both are missing in many responses which causes TS errors during our build. Example input that used to work:

Prompt:
```
# Generate a TypeScript client function to create a user
export async function createUser(payload: CreateUserPayload): Promise<User> {
  // call to API
}
```

Model output (current):
```
async function createUser(payload) {
  fetch('/users', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) })
} // <--- no export, no types
```

TS error we see when building:
```
error TS2304: Cannot find name 'CreateUserPayload'.
error TS2668: Exported variable 'createUser' has or is using private name 'CreateUserPayload'.
```

This started right after you rolled the new model. Can you roll back or advise?
--- end customer message ---

maya_eng: thanks — can you attach the request id and the exact model param they used? also which API (chat vs completions) and any truncation/stop tokens set?

oliver_cs: request id: req_0a9f3c2b (sent 2026-01-12T03:21:44Z). They hit the completions endpoint with model=codegen-2.3q, max_tokens=512, stop sequence ["###"]. No streaming.

trent_ml: do we have the deploy timeline? deploy-bot, @deploy-bot, did the canary fully promote?

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: model codegen-2.3q promoted to default for "codegen" alias at 2026-01-12T03:14:00Z. Canary window: 45m, config id: rollout-20260112-3.

trent_ml: possible culprits: 1) tokenizer changes or punctuation handling causing truncation of trailing exports, 2) prompt-conditioned style shift in the updated weights, 3) a change in default generation params (temperature/stop handling) or a bug in streaming/truncation that chops the tail. Given they used stop sequences, check whether the model treats the stop tokens differently now (strip vs include) and whether the last token got removed.

maya_eng: can repro locally? oliver_cs can you repro with the exact prompt + model using internal test account and attach raw model output?

oliver_cs: repro done. Raw response (trimmed):
```
{
  "id": "resp_zzz",
  "model": "codegen-2.3q",
  "choices": [
    {
      "text": "async function createUser(payload) {\n  await fetch('/users', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) })\n}\n",
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ]
}
```

oliver_cs: note: previous model (codegen-2.2) returned:
```
export async function createUser(payload: CreateUserPayload): Promise<User> {
  // implementation
}
export const helperToNormalize = (x: any) => ({ /* ... */ })
```

trent_ml: that looks like truncation/format drift. Steps:
- compare tokenization for the prompt across 2.2 vs 2.3q (token counts + boundaries)
- replay request with streaming=true to see where finish_reason is set and whether we hit max_tokens early
- check generation params override at alias layer (did alias add a default stop or adjust max_tokens?)
- run a small eval suite of 50 prompts to measure "export" occurrence rate diff between versions

karen_support: created ticket CS-4237, P2, assigned to trent_ml. I recommended rollback to codegen-2.2 for the affected customer tenant while we investigate.

maya_eng: i'll run the tokenization diff and the 50-prompt eval now, will post summary in this thread. If we confirm truncation, we should hotfix the alias config or push a quick rollback per karen.

oliver_cs: customer asked if we can provide a temp workaround — suggested they set model=codegen-2.2 or add a post-processing step to ensure exported function wrappers, but they'd prefer we fix it.

trent_ml: good. also add check for stop-token semantics in the 2.3q model code (maybe different special token IDs). i'll start by fetching model metadata and the rollout manifest for rollout-20260112-3.

maya_eng: update in ~30m with initial eval numbers.

oliver_cs: thanks team :thumbsup: I forwarded the rollback option to Acme and they prefer rollback asap.

karen_support: noting SLA impact — customer build pipeline is blocked. marking high visibility and CC'ing account exec.

maya_eng: quick note — if rollout included a tokenizer patch, that would explain missing type annotations (they are token heavy). prioritizing tokenization diff first.

trent_ml: setting up a dedicated channel for the incident if needed.
